address_pool_gap.description:
Number of consecutive unused addresses allowed.

**IMPORTANT DISCLAIMER:** Using values other than `20` automatically makes your wallet invalid with regards to BIP-44 address discovery. It means that you **will not** be able to fully restore
your wallet in a different software which is strictly following BIP-44.

Beside, using large gaps is **not recommended** as it may induce important performance degradations. Use at your own risks.

**IMPORTANT DISCLAIMER 2:** There is no way to `import` addresses generated outside (e.g. using cardano-addresses) into the wallet.
Wallet only discovers transactions on its used and unused addresses that are within its currently seen `address_pool_gap`.
Transactions on addresses that "belong" to the wallet but happen to be beyond its `address_pool_gap` will not be visible to the wallet.
This is a technical limitation of the industry standard [BIP-44](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0044.mediawiki). See also [CIP-1852](https://github.com/cardano-foundation/CIPs/blob/master/CIP-1852/CIP-1852.md).

metadata.description:
**⚠️ WARNING ⚠️**

_Please note that metadata provided in a transaction will be
stored on the blockchain forever. Make sure not to include any sensitive data,
in particular personally identifiable information (PII)._

Extra application data attached to the transaction.

Cardano allows users and developers to embed their own
authenticated metadata when submitting transactions. Metadata can
be expressed as a JSON object with some restrictions:

1. All top-level keys must be integers between `0` and `2^64 - 1`.

2. Each metadata value is tagged with its type.

3. Strings must be at most 64 bytes when UTF-8 encoded.

4. Bytestrings are hex-encoded, with a maximum length of 64 bytes.

Metadata aren't stored as JSON on the Cardano blockchain but are
instead stored using a compact binary encoding (CBOR).

The binary encoding of metadata values supports three simple types:

* Integers in the range `-(2^64 - 1)` to `2^64 - 1`
* Strings (UTF-8 encoded)
* Bytestrings

And two compound types:

* Lists of metadata values
* Mappings from metadata values to metadata values

It is possible to transform any JSON object into this schema.

However, if your application uses floating point values, they will
need to be converted somehow, according to your
requirements. Likewise for `null` or `bool` values. When reading
metadata from chain, be aware that integers may exceed the
javascript numeric range, and may need special "bigint" parsing.

outputs.description:
A list of target outputs with amounts specified.

When creating a new transaction, the wallet software ensures that all
user-specified transaction outputs have ada amounts that satisfy the ledger
minimum UTxO rule:

- If a user-specified transaction output has an ada `amount` that is
  **zero**, the wallet software will automatically assign a minimal amount
  of ada to the output so that it satisfies the ledger minimum UTxO rule.

- If a user-specified transaction output has an ada `amount` that is
  **non-zero**, the wallet software will verify that the specified amount
  is large enough to satisfy the ledger minimum UTxO rule. If the amount is
  not large enough, the wallet software will return a `utxo_too_small`
  error, together with a revised ada amount that does satisfy the minimum
  UTxO rule.

outputs.description:
A list of target outputs with amounts specified.

When creating a new transaction, the wallet software ensures that all
user-specified transaction outputs have ada amounts that satisfy the ledger
minimum UTxO rule:

- If a user-specified transaction output has an ada `amount` that is
  **zero**, the wallet software will automatically assign a minimal amount
  of ada to the output so that it satisfies the ledger minimum UTxO rule.

- If a user-specified transaction output has an ada `amount` that is
  **non-zero**, the wallet software will verify that the specified amount
  is large enough to satisfy the ledger minimum UTxO rule. If the amount is
  not large enough, the wallet software will return a `utxo_too_small`
  error, together with a revised ada amount that does satisfy the minimum
  UTxO rule.

x-restorationMode.description:
The wallet restoration mode determines since when the wallet should
be restored from the blockchain.

cardano-wallet uses so-called `ChainSync` protocol under the hood to
scan the chain and restore its state from blocks and transactions.
[Ogmios](https://ogmios.dev/mini-protocols/local-chain-sync/) documentation provides a detailed
explanation of this underlying process.

oneOf.description:
Restore the wallet from the genesis block. This will cause the wallet
to be restored from the very beginning of the blockchain, which is
expected to take a long time (several hours on mainnet).
oneOf.title: Restore from genesis

oneOf.description:
Restore the wallet from the tip of the blockchain. The wallet queries
the current tip of the chain and then starts synchronizing from that point.
It waits for the _next block_ to appear before returning a result, which
on _mainnet_ will take an average of 30 seconds.
oneOf.title: Restore from tip

oneOf.description:
Restore the wallet after a specific _point_ identified by a block hash and
slot number. Note that any transaction which is part of that specified block
won't be restored.

Select stake pool metadata fetching strategy:
  - `none` - metadata is not fetched at all,
  - `direct` - metadata is fetched directly URLs registered on chain,
  - `uri` - metadata is fetched from an external Stake-Pool Metadata Aggregation Server (SMASH)

After update existing metadata will be dropped forcing it to re-sync automatically with the new setting.

x-stakePoolApparentPerformance.description:
Apparent performance of the stake pool over past epochs. This indicator is computed
using data available to the server. In particular, the server can't reliably know the
stake distribution of past epochs without being during those epochs. The performance
are therefore an average measure that is more accurate for servers that are online
often.

The performance is a float with double-precision which is _typically_ within `0` and `1`:

  - `0` means that a pool is not performing well.
  - `1` means that a pool is performing _as expected_.
  - above `1` means the pool is performing beyond expectations.

Pools that are lucky enough to win most of their slots early in the epoch will tend to look
like they're over-performing for a while. Having a wallet regularly connected to the network
would harmonize the performance and give better results.

x-stakePoolCost.description:
Estimated cost set by the pool operator when registering his pool.
This fixed cost is taken from each reward earned by the pool before splitting rewards between stakeholders.

May be omitted if the wallet hasn't found the pool's registration cerificate yet.

x-stakePoolFlags.description:
Various flags applicable to stake pools. Possible flags:

| flag     | description                                                                                                      |
| ---      | ---                                                                                                              |
| delisted | The pool is marked as delisted on a configured SMASH server; metadata for this pool have therefore been dropped. |

x-stakePoolId.description: A unique identifier for the pool.

x-stakePoolMargin.description:
Variable margin on the total reward given to an operator before splitting rewards between stakeholders.

May be omitted if the wallet hasn't found the pool's registration cerificate yet.

x-stakePoolMetadataUrl.description: A URL to the stake pool's website.

non_myopic_member_rewards.description:
The rewards the wallet can expect to receive at the end of an epoch, in the long term, if delegating to
this pool.

For more details, see the
[Design Specification for Delegation and Incentives in Cardano](https://hydra.iohk.io/job/Cardano/cardano-ledger-specs/delegationDesignSpec/latest/download-by-type/doc-pdf/delegation_design_spec)
document.

produced_blocks.description: Number of blocks produced by a given stake pool in its lifetime.

relative_stake.description:
The live pool stake relative to the *total* stake.

For more details, see the section "Relative Stake: Active vs Total" in
[Design Specification for Delegation and Incentives in Cardano](https://hydra.iohk.io/job/Cardano/cardano-ledger-specs/delegationDesignSpec/latest/download-by-type/doc-pdf/delegation_design_spec).

saturation.description:
Saturation-level of the pool based on the desired number of pools aimed by the network.
A value above `1` indicates that the pool is saturated.

The `non_myopic_member_rewards` take oversaturation into account, as specified by the [specs](https://hydra.iohk.io/job/Cardano/cardano-ledger-specs/delegationDesignSpec/latest/download-by-type/doc-pdf/delegation_design_spec).

The saturation is based on the live `relative_stake`. The saturation at the end of epoch e,
will affect the rewards paid out at the end of epoch e+3.

x-stakePoolPledge.description:
Minimal stake amount that a stake pool is willing to honor.

May be omitted if the wallet hasn't found the pool's registration cerificate yet.

x-stakePoolRetirement.description:
The epoch in which a stake pool retires.

May be omitted if the wallet hasn't yet found a retirement certificate
for this stake pool.

x-transactionMetadata.description:
**⚠️ WARNING ⚠️**

_Please note that metadata provided in a transaction will be
stored on the blockchain forever. Make sure not to include any sensitive data,
in particular personally identifiable information (PII)._

Extra application data attached to the transaction.

Cardano allows users and developers to embed their own
authenticated metadata when submitting transactions. Metadata can
be expressed as a JSON object with some restrictions:

1. All top-level keys must be integers between `0` and `2^64 - 1`.

2. Each metadata value is tagged with its type.

3. Strings must be at most 64 bytes when UTF-8 encoded.

4. Bytestrings are hex-encoded, with a maximum length of 64 bytes.

Metadata aren't stored as JSON on the Cardano blockchain but are
instead stored using a compact binary encoding (CBOR).

The binary encoding of metadata values supports three simple types:

* Integers in the range `-(2^64 - 1)` to `2^64 - 1`
* Strings (UTF-8 encoded)
* Bytestrings

And two compound types:

* Lists of metadata values
* Mappings from metadata values to metadata values

It is possible to transform any JSON object into this schema.

However, if your application uses floating point values, they will
need to be converted somehow, according to your
requirements. Likewise for `null` or `bool` values. When reading
metadata from chain, be aware that integers may exceed the
javascript numeric range, and may need special "bigint" parsing.

x-transactionOutputs.description:
A list of target outputs with amounts specified.

When creating a new transaction, the wallet software ensures that all
user-specified transaction outputs have ada amounts that satisfy the ledger
minimum UTxO rule:

- If a user-specified transaction output has an ada `amount` that is
  **zero**, the wallet software will automatically assign a minimal amount
  of ada to the output so that it satisfies the ledger minimum UTxO rule.

- If a user-specified transaction output has an ada `amount` that is
  **non-zero**, the wallet software will verify that the specified amount
  is large enough to satisfy the ledger minimum UTxO rule. If the amount is
  not large enough, the wallet software will return a `utxo_too_small`
  error, together with a revised ada amount that does satisfy the minimum
  UTxO rule.

any recovery phrase | big enough     | ✓ withdrawal generated

x-transactionTTL.description:
The TTL (time to live) is the time period in which the transaction
will be accepted into node mempools.

After the TTL has lapsed, the transaction is considered
expired. At this point, nodes will give up on broadcasting the
transaction, and the wallet will release the funds allocated to
the transaction so they can be used for other payments.

The TTL should be long enough that the transaction has time to be
propagated through the network and confirmed, but short enough so
that - in the event of failures - UTxO are returned to the wallet
in a timely manner.

The TTL value is given in seconds. It will be converted to a slot
number internally.

If the TTL is not provided for a payment, a reasonable default
value will be used.

x-transactionWithdrawalRequestSelf.description:
When provided, instruments the server to automatically withdraw rewards from the source wallet when they are deemed
sufficient (i.e. they contribute to the balance for at least as much as they cost).

As a consequence, the resulting transaction may or may not have a withdrawal object. Summarizing:

withdrawal field | reward balance | result
---              | ---            | ---
`null`           | too small      | ✓ no withdrawals generated
`null`           | big enough     | ✓ no withdrawals generated
`"self"`         | too small      | ✓ no withdrawals generated
`"self"`         | big enough     | ✓ withdrawal generated

A list of withdrawals from stake addresses. Withdrawal belonging to the wallet
is underlined.

context.description: Used when withdrawal or output is ours.

anyOf.description:
Indicates whether the phase-2 monetary policy script (e.g. Plutus script)
used in the transaction validated or not. Validity may be null if this
transaction was from an era that doesn't support phase-2 monetary policy
scripts, or is a pending transaction (we don't know if validation passed or
failed until the transaction hits the ledger).

x-validationLevel.description:
Script validation level. Required validation sifts off scripts that would not
be accepted by the ledger. Recommended level filters out scripts that do not pass
required validation and additionally when:
  * 'all' is non-empty
  * there are redundant timelocks in a given level
  * there are no duplicated verification keys in a given level
  * 'at_least' coefficient is positive
  * 'all', 'any' are non-empty and `'at_least' has no less elements in the list
     than the coefficient after timelocks are filtered out.

x-walletAddressPoolGap.description:
Number of consecutive unused addresses allowed.

**IMPORTANT DISCLAIMER:** Using values other than `20` automatically makes your wallet invalid with regards to BIP-44 address discovery. It means that you **will not** be able to fully restore
your wallet in a different software which is strictly following BIP-44.

Beside, using large gaps is **not recommended** as it may induce important performance degradations. Use at your own risks.

**IMPORTANT DISCLAIMER 2:** There is no way to `import` addresses generated outside (e.g. using cardano-addresses) into the wallet.
Wallet only discovers transactions on its used and unused addresses that are within its currently seen `address_pool_gap`.
Transactions on addresses that "belong" to the wallet but happen to be beyond its `address_pool_gap` will not be visible to the wallet.
This is a technical limitation of the industry standard [BIP-44](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0044.mediawiki). See also [CIP-1852](https://github.com/cardano-foundation/CIPs/blob/master/CIP-1852/CIP-1852.md).

x-walletAsset.description:
An asset on the Cardano blockchain. An asset is uniquely identified by
its `policy_id` and `asset_name` (together, these form the _asset id_).

Two assets with the same `asset_name` and `policy_id` are
interchangeable. Yet, different assets with a same `policy_id` but
different `asset_name` are treated as separate assets, as are two
assets with the same `asset_name` but different `policy_id`.

asset_name.description:
The asset on-chain type which acts as a sub-identifier within a
policy. Although we call it "asset name", the value needn't be
text, and it could even be empty.

For policies with a single fungible asset item, asset name is
typically an empty string.

This value can be up to 32 bytes of arbitrary data (which is 64
hexadecimal digits).

policy_id.description:
A unique identifier of the asset's monetary policy. The policy
controls how assets of this kind are created and destroyed.

The contents are the blake2b-224 hash of the monetary policy
script, encoded in hexadecimal.

# Executable live-wallet contracts

These contracts describe the assertions shipped with the Rust harness. The pinned Haskell behavior remains authoritative; an exported specification is a review draft. A described profile, a source-supported outcome or an offline harness test is not evidence of live execution. Only the supplied passing reports under the exact current suite fingerprint establish the bounded validation result. Every missing required case or execution failure prevents the644-obligation gate from passing.

The production interface is HTTP. The trusted Haskell cardano-cli is an independent node query driver; wallet CLI compatibility is excluded. Candidate and reference wallet services have separate databases on the same explicitly identified network. Source/environment binding and executable hashes belong in runtime evidence. Published/internal component vectors remain separate proof for exact key derivation, codecs, signatures, fees and seeded selection; a successful live payment cannot replace them.

## Common inputs, accounting and ownership

`live` takes a target API URL, trusted node socket/CLI, network magic, environment and timeout. Basic execution requires exactly one of a dedicated local-cluster faucet or a funded TESTNET mnemonic. Extended profiles require the dedicated faucet. Payment amount is at least2000000 lovelace. New profiles use fresh generated mnemonic material and do not adopt wallets that already exist. The test encryption passphrase is a public fixture, not a user credential.

Each successfully created Shelley, Byron or shared wallet becomes owned immediately upon a201 response with its ID, before further schema assertions. Cleanup attempts deletion of every owned wallet on success and failure. The external signer owns its own fresh private fixture and cleans it independently. Failed cleanup is report evidence and prevents complete conformance. Requests or response bodies, mnemonic material and private keys are excluded from report diagnostics.

For documented API calls, method/path binding, exact expected status and response schema must pass. NoContent responses must be empty. Polling treats transport/schema failures as failures; expected transaction404 while discovery catches up is separately validated. Readiness and balances must reach the required values within the bounded timeout. ADA arithmetic uses checked integer quantities. No failed, unsupported, skipped or unexecuted profile is converted into a pass.

The independent node driver validates advancing block height and exact wallet latest-header hash/height/slot against observed node tips. Payment proof requires node UTxOs with the exact transaction ID, address and total lovelace; native-asset proof additionally reconciles every policy/name/quantity, including empty names, with no unexpected assets. Wallet-reported confirmation alone is insufficient.

## Basic transfer and restoration

The basic profile requires correct network magic, actual block production and independently matching latest headers. It creates a fresh recipient and either restores the explicitly funded sender fixture or creates/funds its own sender. Both wallets must be ready and the sender have adequate available funds.

Construction must return a positive fee and a coin selection conserving inputs = requested outputs + change + fee, with unique inputs and the exact requested amount. Independent CBOR inspection must reproduce the returned body hash, selected input IDs, exact destination and payment amount. Signing with an incorrect passphrase must fail with the pinned error. Successful signing must retain the original body and fee and provide independently valid extended-derived Ed25519 witnesses. Decode and submission IDs must equal the independently computed body hash.

Both source and recipient must discover the confirmed transaction with correct direction, fee and amount. The node must independently confirm the exact recipient output and every change output. Source balance decreases by payment + fee; recipient balance increases by the payment. UTxO snapshot totals and logarithmic histogram bucket counts must match those balances and actual entry amounts.

Deleting and restoring the recipient from the same mnemonic must retain identity, discovered addresses, confirmed balance and transaction fields including inputs, outputs, fee, amount, metadata and insertion data. This proves the shipped restore-from-genesis case; it does not establish restart durability, rollback or restore-from-checkpoint cases.

## Funded family payments and migrations

`--payments` executes the Shelley member of this profile. `--families` selects Icarus, random Byron and Shelley. Each creates an owned fresh source and an owned Shelley destination. Random Byron addresses are generated with the actual hardened-index endpoint; sequential addresses come from the family's address listing.

A source must receive exactly100000000 lovelace from real on-chain funding and report ready available/total balances of that amount. The node must independently confirm funding. The direct cluster faucet's Byron encoding limitation is preserved as a failed historical run; the proposed Shelley-to-Byron bridge remains unapplied pending approval. A passing Shelley-only profile is not evidence of passing Byron spend or migration.

Fee estimates must have positive ordered min/max values. Applicable sequential coin selections must retain the requested destination/amount, have unique inputs, no unintended assets, and conserve ADA with positive fees inside that interval. Deprecated create/send payment must be confirmed with the same fee constraints and exact recipient node output. Sender/destination balances and history must agree.

A complete migration plan must select the entire remaining ADA balance with no leftover assets/ADA, no source change, a nonempty set of selections and total fee equal to the sum of selection fees. Submitted migrations must have the plan's transaction count and total fees, conserve all remaining ADA into the destination, confirm in both histories and produce the exact independently queried destination UTxOs. Source available/total balance must become zero.

## Two-party shared wallets

`--shared` creates two independent pending private shared wallets with identical all-of-two payment/delegation templates and opposite self-cosigner positions. Pending state must be incomplete, omit balance/tip and reject construction403 shared_wallet_incomplete. Exported account keys must be distinct64-byte acct_shared_xvk values.

Reciprocal payment/delegation cosigner patches must retain exact keys. Payment-only patching must not prematurely activate the wallet. Both completed wallets must become ready and derive identical address pools. Both must discover the same real100m-lovelace funding, independently confirmed at the node.

Construction and decode must retain payment/fee/body hash and conserve ADA. The first party's signed body must contain exactly one independently valid vkey witness; submission must fail403 missing_witnesses_in_transaction with detected1 and expected2. The second party must merge a second distinct valid signature while retaining the first and the original body.

The actual native witness script must hash, with its ledger domain prefix, to the funded address's payment credential. It must be exactly all-of-two signature clauses requiring the two independently verified keys. Fully signed submission must return202 with the body hash; both shared wallets must confirm the outgoing transaction and matching fee/balance, the recipient must confirm the incoming amount, and the node must prove the exact output.

## Watch-only external witnesses

`--external-signer` identifies a separate isolated reference wallet service used only for fixtures. Its API evidence never counts as target API conformance. It creates the private owner and exports its actual64-byte account public key. The target creates an account-public-key watch wallet whose identity must be Blake2b160(account key); private-root and watch identities are distinct constructions.

Address pools must match the private owner's. The funding address's payment credential must equal the independent hash of the watch wallet's reported derived payment public key. Watch state must omit passphrase/private-key state. Both services must discover exact real100m-lovelace funds.

The watch wallet constructs and conserves the requested payment, with no initial signatures and the independently inspected exact destination/body/fee. Target signing must fail403 no_root_key. The external owner signs the unchanged body. Independent verification must find the exact single key matching the funded watch payment credential. Target decode/submission must preserve body ID and fee and accept the signed transaction202.

Both services and the recipient must confirm the appropriate history/balances, and the node must prove the exact recipient output. The target must remain without passphrase state after submission. This establishes the external-signing seam; hardware-specific root/child cryptography is established by separate captured component vectors.

## Native minting, burning and binary submission

`--assets` funds an owned Shelley wallet with100m lovelace and creates its policy key. The returned policy ID must equal independent native signature-script CBOR hashing over that actual policy verification key. Wallet construction mints100 empty-name and100 ab12-name tokens. The original CBOR mint map must contain those exact positive policy/name quantities; signatures must preserve the body and include a valid policy witness.

Only that policy witness signature is corrupted. Independent verification must reject it while the body hash and mint map remain unchanged. Actual submission must receive the strict node rejection below, no rejected transaction UTxOs may exist, and wallet funds/assets must remain unchanged. The valid signed mint is then sent as exact binary bytes through postExternalTransaction, requiring documented202/schema and the exact body ID.

Named/default asset queries must report exact policy/name and independently derived CIP14 fingerprints. Wallet available/total asset quantities and UTxO snapshot totals must agree with independently verified node outputs. Actual wallet burn construction/signing/submission then removes all100 empty-name tokens and40 named tokens. Signed CBOR must contain exact negative quantities, leaving exactly60 named tokens and no empty-name balance. Fees must explain all ADA change; every resulting node output must match the independently inspected CBOR.

HTTP body, raw_body and raw_body_hex are mutually exclusive. raw_body_hex must decode strictly and defaults to application/octet-stream. Binary submission sends decoded bytes, not hexadecimal/base64 text. Malformed encodings or conflicting bodies fail before network transmission.

## Concurrent construction and conflicting spends

`--concurrency` starts with one independently confirmed100m-lovelace funding UTxO and a fresh recipient. Two construction requests for distinct amounts are released simultaneously through a barrier. Both must return documented202/schema, use that exact shared input, have distinct body hashes, retain requested amounts and conserve ADA. Construction/signing must not reserve funds. Both signed bodies must retain their hashes, contain one independently valid payment witness and match the funded address's credential.

Two wallet submissions are then released simultaneously. Exactly one must return202 with its own body ID. The loser must be either strict node500 created_invalid_transaction with the exact handler prefix and ConwayMempoolFailure "All inputs are spent. Transaction has probably already been included", or documented403 foreign_transaction after the confirmed winner's spent input has left the wallet's totalUTxO. These are source-grounded scheduling variants, not permission for arbitrary errors or double acceptance/rejection. The observed variant is recorded. Winning ledger confirmation and exact final accounting are required in either case.

The independently confirmed winner must have the correct sender/recipient history and exact node output. The original shared funding reference must be independently absent from node UTxOs. The loser must be absent from recipient UTxOs and sender history. Replaying the distinct losing signed transaction as binary proxy bytes after winning confirmation must receive the same strict all-inputs-spent node500 cause. This is distinct postExternalTransaction response evidence. Failed requests must not reserve funds. Sender balance equals funding minus winning amount and fee; recipient balance equals only the winning amount.

Each winning change output must be independently confirmed at the node, have reported internal role1, and be discovered as that exact used address/derivation path. The sender's snapshot and histogram must reconcile. The profile proves concurrent construction/submission, conflicting-spend rejection and internal-change discovery cases. It does not establish rollback, restart, pending retry/expiry or sequential-gap/random-Byron discovery cases.

## CIP83 metadata encryption and binary history

`--metadata` creates a fresh funded Shelley wallet and an active one-party shared reader. The Shelley wallet constructs metadata-only encryption with public UTF8 message/password fixtures under674.msg, an untouched674.note,64 nonUTF8 bytes under label0 and the maximum u64 label. Encryption must preserve unrelated values and emit the basic method with nonempty base64 chunks of at most64 characters, Salted__ framing, an8-byte salt and block-aligned ciphertext.

Independent parsing verifies the exact Conway auxiliary-data tag259/map0 envelope and its body hash, reconstructs detailed metadata, and re-encodes it with the independently golden-checked Rust metadata encoder. Coin-selection binary metadata must equal the original metadata CBOR bytes. Bounded OpenSSL AES256CBC/PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 with10000 iterations and8-byte salt must decrypt the public message exactly. No Unicode normalization or authenticated-encryption guarantee is assumed for CBC.

Shelley inspection without a password must retain ciphertext; the correct metadata password must recover the complete original detailed metadata, and the wrong password must return documented403 invalid_metadata_decryption. The live successful map places the unchanged int42 note before msg. Fixed-salt Haskell adapter vectors separately retain both map orders and the exact ErrorCall for msg-before-note decryption. Shared inspection without decrypt_metadata must retain ciphertext202. Shared decrypt_metadata must return the observed exact500 text/plain body "Something went wrong", through an approved operation-scoped overlay and strict UTF-8/schema validation; it does not claim shared decryption works.

Signing must retain the exact body and auxiliary data and provide independently verified signatures. Submission and self-transfer confirmation must preserve the exact encrypted/binary history values and fee, conserve the wallet's ADA, and produce independently confirmed node outputs. Other history order/pagination/status/time-range obligations remain separate. This profile uses OpenSSL from the pinned development environment (or an explicitly identified executable); private mnemonic material and crypto inputs are excluded from report diagnostics.
